Kiberdrosibas likums (National Cybersecurity Law) entered into force 1 Sept 2024, but per Advisera and the Commission's own May 2025 reasoned opinion, that framework law alone did not constitute full transposition -- it explicitly delegated the actual minimum requirements to later Cabinet of Ministers regulations. Those regulations -- Ministru kabineta noteikumi Nr. 397, 'Minimalas kiberdrosibas prasibas' (Minimum Cybersecurity Requirements) -- entered into force 2 July 2025, and are described by two independent sources (Lex Mundi's NIS2 implementation guide; Widen legal alert, both found 7 Sept 2026 second pass) as completing Latvia's Art. 41(1) transposition obligation. Used 2 July 2025 as the transposition date -- NOTE this postdates the Commission's 7 May 2025 reasoned opinion, so it's plausible the Commission's public infringement tracker (used for enforcement_tier) has not been updated to reflect this and Latvia may still show as 'reasoned opinion' stage in the DV even though the underlying law is now in force; this is a genuine, worth-flagging tension between the two DVs, not a data error in either one.

Legal Notice 71/2025 (the substantive NIS2 transposition order) published 8 Apr 2025 but explicitly NOT YET IN FORCE as of that publication, pending a ministerial commencement order. That order -- Legal Notice 22 of 2026 -- designated 23 January 2026 as the date all provisions of LN 71/2025 come into force. Confirmed by two independent sources found 7 Sept 2026 second pass: PwC Malta ('Malta's NIS2 Framework comes into force') and a Mondaq legal alert ('NIS2 Transposition Is Now Fully In Force'), both citing 23 Jan 2026 and LN 22/2026 by name. (Note: a separate later instrument, LN 89 of 2026, made further amendments in April 2026 -- an Enforcement Committee, CSIRT relocation -- but is not the commencement instrument; do not confuse the two.)
